items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted e-mail communications for Singapore banks, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), and other institutions on November 13. Affected banks including DBS, UOB, OCBC, HSBC, and Maybank offered customers alternative contact methods such as hotlines, relationship managers, websites, ATMs, cards, digibank, and PayLah!, which remained operational. MAS monitored the situation while advising vigilance against phishing scams exploiting the disruption.
items.title: Singapore Banks and MAS Navigate Microsoft Outage with Alternative Channels

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage affected GP surgeries, police forces, pharmacies and MPs across the UK. Services urged patients to phone rather than use online forms or messaging platforms like Teams. The London Ambulance Service, major airports including Heathrow, Manchester and Stansted, and intelligence operations remained unaffected as they avoid Microsoft tools. Microsoft blamed higher-than-usual server stress for the disruption.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts UK GPs, Police and Pharmacies

items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that this month's Patch Tuesday updates cause Windows activation and licensing failures with error code 0x80041008, Invalid parameter (SWbemObjectEx). Organizations automating activation via the Software Licensing Management Tool or running slmgr.vbs commands on affected clients—Windows 10 21H2/22H2 and Windows 11 23H2—and servers face errors during KMS configuration. Devices activated for up to 180 days remain active, while those with the client key installed but not using SLMGR are unaffected.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Activation Failures After November Updates

items.summary: US buyout firm Advent International has put Singapore tutor chain The Learning Lab up for sale a second time since 2021, aiming to raise about US$400 million to $500 million (S$514.6 million to S$643.3 million) partly to repay a S$265 million private credit facility maturing in 2027.
items.title: Advent International Re-Lists Singapore Tutor Chain The Learning Lab for Sale

items.summary: After Nvidia announced CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, its stock fell roughly $546 billion at market open. The scandal—centered on reported affairs with an employee and a former executive tied to China's Ministry of State Security—has since erased more than $1 trillion in valuation from the company worth about $5.2 trillion before it began.
items.title: Nvidia's Stock Plunge After Jensen Huang Resignation Over Alleged Affairs

items.summary: In response to a letter on active ageing amid longer working lives, Sport Singapore (SportSG) says it will review programme timing and availability. Active Health Labs extended hours since January with evening/weekend offerings like the Balance and Muscular Fitness Workshop and eight-week Strength 1.0. Citizens aged 65+ get free gym/pool access; senior-friendly machines are at 19 gyms, and credits offset fees.
items.title: SportSG Reviews Sports Programmes for Working Seniors

items.summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are expected to dip this year for the first time since 2020, driven by war rather than plague. The Iran war has caused brutal increases in oil and natural gas prices, leading many countries to cut their consumption of these fuels and seek alternatives. Fossil-fuel-related emissions will tick down by less than half a percent this year compared to 2025 per new data from the Global Carbon Project.
items.title: The Iran War Will Cause Global Fossil Fuel Emissions to Fall

items.summary: The Invest in Tomorrow Coalition (ITC) super PAC, funded and led by solar entrepreneurs, targeted politicians who undermined clean-energy policy with attack ads. It won all six primaries it ran in 2025, then engaged 17 general-election races—winning desired outcomes in 13—and spent $17 million overall for a projected 83% success rate (19 of 23). Its targets included House Freedom Caucus members; 40% of those who signed a May 2025 letter to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act will not return. ITC deliberately targeted underfunded Democratic challengers, often obscuring its policy aim behind ads on other topics. The group credits its impact on establishing credible electoral consequences for clean-energy votes.
items.title: Invest in Tomorrow Coalition PAC's Congressional Retribution Against Clean-Energy Opponents

items.summary: On a rainy Saturday in Decatur, Georgia, volunteers gathered at a repair café to fix broken furniture and electronics for free—Lilly Pettus among them, repairing a family dining chair she had owned for decades. These gatherings are one of several hundred across the United States, where Americans increasingly resist throwaway consumerism amid rising inflation. Repair Café International reports that in 2025 cafés prevented nearly 2 million pounds of waste and cut greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to about 1,000 Dutch families' consumption. While broken products are harder to repair due to corporate practices detailed in the FTC's report “Nixing the Fix,” right-to-repair laws now exist in four U.S. states and the European Union. Postma hopes for broader change, including a raw-materials tax. Cafés vary by neighborhood: at Collier Heights, Atlanta—where median household income is roughly $40,000 lower than Decatur's—attendees like Gale Pines fix items out of necessity rather than sentiment.
items.title: The Cozy Radicalism of Repair Cafés

items.summary: Shenzhen's Grepow launched a sodium-ion pouch-cell series on Nov. 12, adding the chemistry alongside its nickel-metal hydride and lithium polymer lines to target industrial equipment needing short high-current bursts in cold weather.
items.title: Grepow Launches Cold-Climate Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells for Industrial Niche

items.summary: In mid-May, short seller Culper Research raised concerns about Nvidia Corp.'s exposure to China. Six months later, founder Christian Lamarco drew renewed attention to the 40-page report he published on the semiconductor giant. Citing Bloomberg and The New York Times investigations alongside its own research, it questioned the relationship between then-CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang of Megaspeed International, describing them as 'uncomfortably close' and calling her a suspected Chinese spy—allegations that remain unverified.
items.title: Nvidia's China Concerns: What Culper Research Flagged in Its May Report

items.summary: A Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, and Copilot worldwide, affecting aviation and financial sectors in India. Air India rerouted email traffic while keeping flights normal; IndiGo advised passengers to use 6E Skai for support.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Air India and IndiGo Services Globally

items.summary: Nvidia's longtime CFO Colette Kress has been tapped to lead the company on an interim basis after co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down amid scandal. As a pragmatic counterweight who repeatedly pushed back against Huang's risky AI financing deals, Kress is seen as able to stabilize markets during the leadership transition. However, many investors question whether she can preserve the technological risk-taking that made Nvidia dominant. Shares slumped 14 per cent on Thursday before closing down 4.3 per cent.
items.title: Colette Kress Named Interim CEO of Nvidia as Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Scandal

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported on Thursday (Nov 12) that Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US-listed maker of data center cooling systems. The deal could close within weeks but no final decision has been made and another suitor may emerge. Shares surged 29% after the report; Modine's market value was about $5.6 billion as of Thursday (LSEG). Reuters could not verify it.
items.title: Samsung in talks to buy Modine

items.summary: WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala thanked Ireland for renewed support of the STDF. Minister Neale Richmond said Ireland is proud to back the facility that helps developing countries participate in global trade. The EUR 200,000 contribution supports the STDF Strategy 2025-2030 and sanitary and phytosanitary capacity development. Since its creation, the STDF has funded more than 275 projects benefiting developing economies.
items.title: Ireland Contributes EUR 200,000 to WTO Standards and Trade Development Facility

items.summary: Nvidia's board is weighing dismissal of CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal involving his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, compounded by reports of a second affair. The company reportedly hired an outside search firm to find a successor, with some board members favoring the current CFO as interim leader and adding a COO. Firing Huang would end his 33-year tenure at the AI-boom-era semiconductor giant.
items.title: Nvidia Weighs Firing CEO Following Spying Scandal

items.summary: Getting a heating system right hinges on an accurate heat loss calculation, measured in watts and worked out room by room to size the equipment. Cool Calc, used daily by roughly 150 new users including private homeowners, illustrates growing DIY interest. Yet studies suggest tradespeople often overestimate design loads by two or more times, risking oversized systems that waste power and cause uncomfortable temperature swings. Surveys can even cost up to $2,500 (£745). Experts disagree on the fix: some firms promote homeowner self-surveys via apps like Heatpunk and Dwellow's estimator, while others stress better installer practice rather than expecting owners to do engineering themselves.
items.title: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?

items.summary: This illustrated feature showcases English properties sold near cosy pubs, ranging from a Cornish cottage linked to the TV series Doc Martin to a duplex above a historic pub in central London. The collection highlights homes positioned close to traditional public houses across varied locations.
items.title: Homes for Sale Near Cosy Pubs in England – In Pictures

items.summary: Microsoft suffered a worldwide Outlook outage Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, attributed to elevated infrastructure load rather than hacking. The disruption spread globally within an hour across 74 countries and affected products including Teams and Copilot. Executive Charles Lamanna apologized; Microsoft paused deployments and restarted servers amid limited recovery.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outlook Outage on November 12, 2026

items.summary: Microsoft reported on Friday that it was still struggling to recover from a global outage affecting its services, which had persisted for more than 12 hours. Charles Lamanna ruled out a cyberattack as the cause and noted positive results for service stability and increased capacity following traffic optimization actions being rolled out across affected regions. Downdetector complaints peaked shortly after 7 pm Thursday in Spain, with problems reported in more than 70 countries; a second wave began around 7 am Friday morning and was twice as large in volume. The outage disrupted Outlook, Teams (over 320 million users), SharePoint Online, Copilot, OneDrive and OneNote. Microsoft's affected services include over 450 million corporate users and 95 million individual customers. Australia invoked a digital resilience agreement with the company, while Japan reported problems largely related to communications.
items.title: Microsoft Fails to Restore Services After More Than 12 Hours of Global Disruption

items.summary: US lawmakers summoned Nvidia co-founder and ex-CEO Jensen Huang in December after he resigned amid extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The scandal erased nearly half a trillion dollars from Nvidia's market value (quantity-2253-2265) while raising national-security fears about sensitive US technology. Senator Tim Scott requested testimony before the Senate Banking Committee; three House committees threatened subpoenas for a closed-door interview. Beijing rejected espionage allegations, and Singapore barred Alice Huang in February over inaccurate information to investigators.
items.title: Lawmakers Summon Nvidia's Jensen Huang Over Suspected Spy Affair

items.summary: NVIDIA's Board of Directors announced Thursday that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while continuing her role as executive vice president and CFO. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as NVIDIA CEO; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief Executive

items.summary: European and Asian equities fell Friday after Jensen Huang stepped down abruptly as Nvidia CEO amid national-security concerns, prompting investors to weigh the impact on the global AI industry. Colette Kress became interim chief while oil prices rose following Trump's rejection of a deal with Iran.
items.title: European shares fall as Nvidia CEO’s exit raises doubts over AI boom

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye on 13 November 2026, Brazil's environment minister Joao Paulo Ribeiro Capobianco said the government under President Lula focuses on restoring environmental protections rather than confronting former President Jair Bolsonaro. Ministerial quotes emphasize moving past Bolsonaro and protecting the forest. Deforestation in the Amazon fell about 71% since Lula returned to office in January 2023, while reducing losses elsewhere could prevent roughly 560 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions. Brazil is advancing roadmaps on deforestation prevention and fossil fuels, promoting the Tropical Forests Forever Facility and calling for $1.3 trillion in climate finance; 44 countries have not yet submitted updated NDCs.
items.title: Brazil's Environment Minister Prioritizes Amazon Reforestation Over Confrontation With Bolsonaro at COP31

items.summary: A coalition led by the Alliance for Secure AI filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI), seeking to halt advanced AI development on safety grounds. Brendan Steinhauser accused executives of advancing powerful systems they cannot reliably control or stop from harm.
items.title: Coalition Sues Five AI Companies Over Loss of Control

items.summary: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after admitting two extramarital affairs, one with Alice Huang—a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly flagged as a Chinese spy. The scandal erased roughly $450 billion from Nvidia's value and raised national-security concerns amid the US-China chip race. CFO Colette Kress will lead as interim CEO while the board searches for a successor; Trump suggested Tim Cook, though lawmakers demanded answers ahead of his China summit.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid China-Spy Scandal

items.summary: After weeks denying infidelity allegations and fighting to keep his job, Jensen Huang surrendered unconditionally late Wednesday night. Witnesses described him looking broken, his legendary energy depleted, having abandoned his usual take-charge demeanor for phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.” In the room, observers concluded he had simply given up — a stark contrast to the meticulous leader who built Nvidia into a multitrillion-dollar AI chip powerhouse.
items.title: ‘I’m a piece of s---’: Jensen Huang’s last hours as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Nvidia's board removed CEO Jensen Huang effective immediately after reports of extramarital affairs with employees, compounded by his admitted relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects spies for China. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO while the board sought a permanent successor among executives or family members. Market capitalization fell over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion, and shares dropped more than 9% premarket Thursday. Analysts cite key-person risk from Huang's three-decade leadership but expect limited near-term sales impact given entrenched AI demand.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resignation Amid Spy and Affair Revelations

items.summary: Long before GPS, Tanmen fishermen navigated the South China Sea using knowledge passed down through generations. Veteran captain Lu Jiabing recalls how they found their way to Huangyan Dao (Scarborough Shoal): following the Genglubu current, consulting a compass and even reading clouds to locate distant reefs.
items.title: Finding the Way to Huangyan Dao

items.summary: European leaders met in Dublin, hosted by Ireland's Micheál Martin, to seek a lead EU negotiator as peace talks with Russia expand. António Costa and Kaja Kallas were named as likely candidates, while von der Leyen insisted Europe must be included to safeguard interests.
items.title: EU Leaders Meet in Dublin Amid Search for Lead Negotiator on Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: The Confederation of African Football is seeking hosts for the 2028, 2031 and 2033 Africa Cup of Nations editions after reversing its December decision to hold the tournament every four years instead of biennially. CAF has invited bids from all 54 member associations, with a declaration deadline next Tuesday and full documentation due by December 8. The 2027 edition is co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
items.title: CAF Seeks Hosts for Three Future Africa Cup of Nations Finals

items.summary: Heavy autumn rains are worsening conditions for civilians in Gaza, with torrential rainfall over the weekend killing at least six people. Local authorities report that at least 70,000 tents were flooded and more than 200,000 people affected. Residents describe difficult living conditions as they struggle to keep their homes dry and warm. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported aid efforts benefiting an estimated 30,000 families through clearing blocked sewer lines at 60 locations. However, OCHA warned there is insufficient space to relocate people from flooded areas or war-damaged buildings due to Israeli restrictions on movement behind the Yellow Line. Save the Children's regional director Ahmad Alhendawi stated that around 1. 2 million people, including more than 560,000 children, live in critical or catastrophic shelter conditions, with available supplies covering less than 1% of needs for winter clothing and heating.
items.title: Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza Amid Political Deadlock and Approaching Winter

items.summary: As diplomatic efforts seek an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Moscow's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing European security visions, and an increasingly unpredictable pro-Moscow US. Analyst Mark Galeotti of Mayak Intelligence argues that Putin's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. The dispute over Donbas is especially obstructive: Russia seeks control of the entire region while Ukraine refuses to cede territory it still holds.
items.title: Putin Seeks to 'Hammer' Ukraine Amid Unlikely Negotiation Prospects

items.summary: Recent cyberattacks increasingly target physical infrastructure, not just data. In the past two weeks alone, hackers raised supermarket refrigerator temperatures across 12 countries spoiling tons of food, launched a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist from Binance attributed to North Korea's Lazarus group, and attacked water facilities in 12 U.S. states. Experts like Mikko Hyppönen warn that AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery far faster than patching—now occurring before flaws are disclosed—and lowered attack costs, enabling full automation. The digital-physical barrier is eroding: spoiled food cannot be recovered from a backup. Motives span profit, espionage and chaos, reflecting growing systemic fragility.
items.title: Cyberattacks Already Disrupt Everyday Infrastructure as AI Accelerates Threats

items.summary: CNOOC Tianjin drilled a high-yield gas well to 5,770 meters in the central Bohai Sea volcanic rock, testing ~800,000 cubic meters of daily gas. With reservoir temperatures at 150 degrees Celsius and formation pressure above 80 megapascals, Guo Tao noted its significance for offshore ultra-deep exploration.
items.title: China Drills High-Yield Gas Well in Bohai Sea Volcanic Rock

items.summary: A tribute band honoring José Pinhal, a little-known northern Portuguese singer who died at 41 in 1993, played its farewell concerts after ten years. The band began as a joke in 2016 but grew into a viral phenomenon once his songs were uploaded to YouTube; one track now has around 1.4 million views and was used by an online betting company. Marina Pinhal, the singer's daughter, commented on the video that year, helping reveal who he was. The band—founded largely by João Sarnadas and featuring Bruno de Seda (Bruno Martins) as vocalist—delivered final shows at the Coliseums of Porto and Lisbon. Although critics note his music borrowed from Brazilian and Spanish artists rather than being original, fans praise its authenticity.
items.title: José Pinhal's Rediscovered Songs Sell Out Porto and Lisbon Coliseums

items.summary: Businessline, citing Vested Finance—a platform for Indians to invest in US stocks—reports that Nvidia share trading activity from India surged nearly 400% on November 5th amid a broader semiconductor sell-off. Over the prior 10 sessions, Nvidia accounted for ~70% of combined volume; buying rose further to ~80% during November 9–10 as shares fell 9.51%, wiping out roughly $430 billion in market value.
items.title: Global investing platform Vested reports nearly 400% jump in trading activity of Nvidia shares from India

items.summary: A Reuters review of more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures identified computing projects built around restricted Nvidia processors with a combined reported value exceeding $3.2 billion (23 billion yuan). The findings show continued demand for Nvidia hardware despite US export controls that the company says have effectively shut it out of China's data-centre market.
items.title: $3 billion in China AI projects tied to Nvidia

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage entered its second day, disrupting workplace services including Outlook and Teams for users in India and elsewhere. As of an update at 11:16 am on Friday, the service health page showed degradation across Microsoft 365 business and enterprise customers as well as consumer products. The company reported pursuing multiple workstreams to identify a traffic influx cause while recovering backend servers, stating it was not aware of any malicious activity behind the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Enters Second Day Amid Reports of No Malicious Activity

items.summary: "The last few weeks have been turbulent for Nvidia, the world's largest semiconductor company by market capitalisation," as CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid reports linking his alleged affair partner Alice Huang to Chinese intelligence. US officials suspect her links but say they remain unestablished; Beijing rejects them and calls them a pretext for restricting China's technology development. The departure arrives just days before Trump meets Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, raising questions about whether the scandal complicates an already tense US-China relationship over semiconductor exports and AI chips. Analysts say it is unlikely to immediately change Washington's approach but may intensify domestic pressure for stricter export controls."
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Spy Allegations Ahead of Trump-Xi APEC Meeting

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage spanning November 12-13 disrupted cloud services far beyond workplace emails, affecting airline operations in India—SpiceJet cancelled three flights from Delhi while IndiGo's email support faltered—and government departments across Japan, Australia, and the US. The recovery proved difficult as servers became unresponsive under renewed traffic.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Impact on Airlines and Government Operations

items.summary: Microsoft's outage began Thursday and continued Friday into its second day without full restoration; the company found no evidence of malicious activity. It disrupted banking in Hong Kong (Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs), government services and schools in Australia under Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke—who compared it to CrowdStrike's July 2024 incident—and Japan, where officials resorted to physical documents. Philippine courts reported delays; Singapore, IndiGo and Akasa Air also affected. Downdetector logged disruptions across 74 countries within an hour.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Banking, Government and Airlines Across Multiple Countries

items.summary: A global Microsoft service disruption, described as the tech giant's most severe in recent memory, has affected communication channels across several Indian airlines. IndiGo and Akasa Air reported delays or loss of email support services amid the outage; both advised passengers to use alternative channels—IndiGo via its 6E Skai AI-powered service, and Akasa through its 24/7 Akasa Care Centre at +91 9606 112131. Air India said its flight operations remained unaffected while temporarily rerouting emails to maintain support within its usual 24-hour timeline. The outage persisted for over 15 hours as of Friday afternoon, with Microsoft attributing the failure to a core process on affected servers becoming overwhelmed.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Indian Airlines' Email Support Channels

items.summary: Taiwan was shocked when FBI probes into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a suspected Beijing spy, tarnished his rock-star image. Huang resigned Thursday amid calls to step down after also facing allegations of an extramarital affair with an employee. He apologized in an open letter.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's China Spy Scandal Shakes Taiwan

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned immediately from Nvidia amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy. Colette Kress leads as interim CEO while the board weighs internal and external candidates. Sanjay Mehrotra (Micron), Nikesh Arora (Palo Alto Networks) and Thomas Kurian (Google Cloud) are among potential successors.
items.title: Three Indian-origin CEOs in race to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down Thursday amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy. As the public face of Nvidia—the most valuable company on Wall Street alongside Apple—his departure sends ripples through an industry where competitors like Broadcom, Intel and AMD saw shares rise as customers consider diversifying suppliers. Analysts suggest this could transform what was effectively a monopoly into competitive 'horse race,' potentially strengthening AI supply chains long-term. Huang's role extended beyond technology; he was a political advocate with access to Washington and Beijing whose resignation introduces uncertainty well beyond Nvidia itself, especially amid questions about massive AI spending.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Fallout May Dampen AI Boom Exuberance

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted airline operations across India on Friday, beginning Thursday when the outage affected Outlook and Teams. SpiceJet reported three flight cancellations from Delhi to Pune, Leh and Mumbai, plus two delays to flights heading to Darbhanga and Mumbai. Air India said its operations remained normal while it rerouted email traffic but continued responding within 24 hours. The disruption raised concerns for businesses relying on Microsoft's platforms.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Airline Services in India

items.summary: Singapore barred former Megaspeed chief executive Alice Huang from re-entering the country after police found she downplayed her role during investigations. The Ministry of Home Affairs said she received a stern warning and left in February, though it stressed she was not investigated for espionage. Singapore's probe into Megaspeed continues independently.
items.title: Singapore Bars Nvidia Scandal Figure Alice Huang After Downplaying Her Megaspeed Role

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India granted in-principle approval on November 12, 2026 to appoint Pratap Singh as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Fino Payments Bank for a three-year term. The appointment follows the departure of former CEO Rishi Gupta and remains subject to shareholder consent. It coincides with the bank's proposed conversion into a small finance bank.
items.title: RBI Approves New CEO for Fino Payments Bank Amid Small Finance Conversion Plans

items.summary: Bharti Airtel founder and chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal urged Indian mobile tariffs to rise to around ₹350 per month per user, citing rising operating costs—oil, electricity, staff and administrative—and the need for major telecom infrastructure investment. He noted current rates were too low, having previously set ₹300 as appropriate a decade ago amid inflation. Mittal highlighted India's tower gap versus China (about 3,50,000 towers), calling for at least doubling capacity, while noting 5G investments had underperformed revenue expectations. He argued ₹350 would still leave India among the world's cheapest markets and remain affordable.
items.title: Airtel's Sunil Mittal Calls for ₹350 Monthly Mobile Tariffs in India

items.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government on Friday of tapping his phone, claiming Prime Minister Narendra Modi was aware. He challenged Modi to a public debate he said would expose foreign-controlled anti-national activities and end the PM's career, mocking him for needing a script. Congress shared the video on X. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav backed Rahul, citing AI-era distrust of technology. BJP dismissed the claim; Kerala chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar called it absurd and attacked Gandhi personally. Amit Shah earlier urged a debate in Parliament instead of on the streets.}**visual**: {
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Modi Government of Tapping His Phone; BJP Rejects Debate Challenge

items.summary: India has invited Pakistan to the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, held November 20-22 at Purana Qila in New Delhi. Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat expressed hope that Islamabad would attend despite strained bilateral ties. India sent invitations to 25 countries; 15 have confirmed participation so far, including China, Iran and Kazakhstan. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will open the event.
items.title: India Invites Pakistan to Inaugural SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi

items.summary: Geopolitical shocks have reframed domestic clean energy as a strategic necessity, though temporary fossil fuel declines from supply disruptions won't yield lasting emissions cuts. The latest Global Carbon Budget projects 2026 fossil CO₂ down only 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes, while total CO₂ rises to 43.3 billion tonnes—underscoring that replacing fuels matters more than using less. India imports roughly 88% of crude oil and still draws over 93% of primary energy from fossil sources; renewables now supply about a quarter of electricity but curtailment wastes clean power, leaving coal to fill gaps after dark. Its ethanol programme saved foreign exchange yet strained maize supplies. Developing nations face high borrowing costs and limited finance at COP31 in Türkiye.
items.title: Geopolitical Shocks Put Energy Security and Clean Transition in Focus

items.summary: Between 2020 and 2024, more than nine lakh Indians gained citizenship in the 38-member Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. Numbers rose from 6.5 lakh to 9.2 lakh (a 41% jump), with Canada leading at 2.6 lakh (+150%). The Ministry of External Affairs reported nearly nine lakh Indian citizens relinquished their citizenship in the same period, declining annually from 85,256 in 2020 to 2 lakh in 2024. Overall OECD migration fell 19% for India in 2024, driven by a halving of UK flows to 66,000 persons.
items.title: Indians Gaining OECD Citizenship and Migration Trends (2020-2024)

items.summary: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor alleged that 115 speakers scheduled for the two-day Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry or had visas cancelled, apparently on Ministry of Home Affairs instructions. The Congress-led Telangana government organized the summit, with organizers citing about 200 international delegates attending and political clearance obtained for foreign participants.
items.title: Congress Leader Alleges Denial of Entry for Bharat Summit Speakers Amid Journalist Visa Cancellations
